categories.name: Static Clicking
categories.headline: Still targets. Time between kills.
categories.description: Targets stationary. Score = gap between kills. One large initial flick → one small micro-correction → click. Straight line target to target, no overflick. During micro, next target already located in peripheral.

categories.name: Dynamic Clicking
categories.headline: Read. Confirm. Commit.
categories.description: Follow the movement into each shot. Read arcs beyond the apex and stay with multi-hit targets until the final click. Smooth transitions make the next target easier to read.

categories.name: Precise Tracking
categories.headline: Stay connected.
categories.description: Match the target through horizontal strafes, vertical travel and changing paths. Make clean corrections when contact breaks. Use an easier cut when you lose the movement; difficulty should leave room to learn.

categories.name: Reactive Tracking
categories.headline: React, recover, settle.
categories.description: Watch the target, react to the change, then match its new movement. Stops and teleports join ground and air reads. If you start guessing turns or forcing the mouse, step down and rebuild clean contact.

categories.name: Speed Switching
categories.headline: Find pace. Keep precision.
categories.description: Hold fire, land close and finish each target before transferring. Mix compact flicks, wide routes and shrinking targets. In practice, try a short speed burst on an easier cut; use complete runs for benchmark scores.

categories.name: Evasive Switching
categories.headline: Earn every transfer.
categories.description: Flick in, match the movement and confirm the kill. Read the next target without abandoning this one. Regeneration tests clean finishes; varied arcs and strafes keep the task about reading, not memorising turns.

thresholds.note: Every threshold in this file is an authored score read from data/pool.json, not a percentile of anybody's population. A percentile moves when the population moves, so the target slides while somebody is chasing it, and a benchmark for improvement wants a number that sits still. Each one carries a `source` saying whether it was adopted verbatim from a published benchmark, reconciled between several, authored outright with a reason, or is still seeded - inherited from the percentile era and not yet given a source. npm run validate:thresholds re-derives the first two and counts the last.

boards.note: The boards no longer set the thresholds; they audit them. Each scenario carries `sanity.clears` - what share of that leaderboard meets each rank - which is how a threshold nobody can reach, or one everybody clears, gets caught now that no percentile guarantees it by construction.
